decisions.reason: As a large R&D-active machinery firm with slack and long industrial sales cycles, it is likely to retain this core-adjacent coolant system extension while learning about demand and bundling it with established offers.

The centrifuge fits the firm's established coolant-management capabilities and service model, so early uncertainty is unlikely to trigger withdrawal within a year unless results are clearly far below aspiration.

Coolant nozzles are a close complementary product line with several models, and such modular add-ons are typically kept because they support system sales and can be adjusted without exiting the market.

Although somewhat less embedded than the core coolant products, the scraper belt chip conveyor remains close to the firm's conveying portfolio and a large incumbent would usually give it more time before redeploying resources.
This magnetic belt chip conveyor builds directly on existing conveying know-how and customer needs, making continued offering more likely than rapid withdrawal under bounded-rational learning.

The hinged belt chip conveyor is near the established business and likely part of a broad solution portfolio, so management would usually keep it unless early feedback clearly underperforms aspiration levels.
